items.note: Within-subjects study: 31 online creative-writing students did the same exercise with no ChatGPT, ChatGPT alone, and ChatGPT plus instructor guidance; expert judges scored creativity with the Consensual Assessment Technique; abstract does not say whether condition order was randomized; below the 50-person threshold.

Sixteen students in two groups prepared weekly materials using only AI chatbots versus any resource except chatbots; creative skills and critical thinking were weaker in the chatbot group; unclear whether creativity was scored on the essays; below the 50-person threshold.

92 male EFL learners in high-AI-feedback, low-AI-feedback, and conventional-instruction groups, with pre- and posttest creative writing; abstract does not state assignment method (one search lane read computer-generated random assignment in the text) or whether AI was available at posttest (possible after_ai).

40 design students randomly assigned to two groups; phase 1 with versus without a text-to-image tool, phase 2 both without AI (after_ai carry-over); professionals rated designs on the Creative Product Semantic Scale; below the 50-person threshold.

Proposes the GPS prompting framework for brainstorming with an LLM, tested through a design example and a case study with TTCT-adapted scoring of AI-generated ideas; no comparison condition in the abstract; abstract taken from the arXiv preprint version (arXiv 2410.11877), the journal abstract was not reachable.

SSRN abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, SSRN page all failed); the first author's MSU dissertation abstract describes a quasi-experiment varying LLM randomness during human-LLM writing, with perceived creativity of the work as outcome; full text needed to check assignment and N.

Experiment with professional illustrators in which AI assistance flattens the quality curve of their artworks and many stop early; the short Crossref abstract gives no N or assignment (a university bulletin reports 219 artists, 168 randomly allowed GenAI in a second session).

Within-subjects experiment with 62 Chinese university students comparing personalised versus standard GenAI feedback (ai_design) on the quality and elaboration of creative problem-solving solutions; abstract does not say whether condition order was randomized.

Controlled experiment varying the variance of AI-generated design sets and recording which designs participants select; the outcome is diversity of selections among AI outputs, not of participant-made output, so it may fail the outcome criterion; no no-AI arm and N not stated.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Springer page all failed); title suggests an intervention study of GenAI-based creative-thinking training on fine arts students' artistic creativity, included in a meta-analysis; design, comparison group, and N unknown.
